name: Hangout Shows
tagline: Where everybody knows your name... or at least your coffee order.
description: Ensemble casts anchored to a central gathering spot. Friendship-as-family dynamics. The location is a character.

source.description: Big Bang Theory Fandom Wiki - Sheldon's Knock

questions.questionText: In How I Met Your Mother, what elaborate theory does Barney use to pick up women, involving a visual aid?
How much did each Friends cast member earn per episode in the final two seasons?
questions.funFact: The cast collectively negotiated their salaries together, refusing to let the network pay anyone more than the others.

questions.questionText: What address is the Friends apartment building exterior located at in Greenwich Village?
questions.funFact: The building at 90 Bedford Street became such a tourist attraction that the owners had to put up barriers to keep fans away.

questions.questionText: How many viewers watched the Friends series finale?
questions.funFact: Stage 24 at Warner Bros. Studios was renamed 'The Friends Stage' after filming wrapped.

questions.questionText: What is Joey Tribbiani's signature pickup line on Friends?
options: Did it hurt when you fell from heaven?
questions.funFact: Matt LeBlanc improvised 'How you doin'?' in an early episode. The writers loved it so much they made it Joey's permanent catchphrase.

questions.questionText: What is the theme song of Cheers called?
questions.funFact: Gary Portnoy wrote the song. It became so iconic that the real Bull & Finch Pub in Boston renamed itself 'Cheers' to capitalize on tourism.

questions.questionText: What do the bar patrons yell every time Norm Peterson walks into Cheers?
questions.funFact: George Wendt improvised a different one-liner response each time, creating over 200 unique 'Norm entrances' across the series.

questions.questionText: Which Cheers character got their own spin-off series set in Seattle?
questions.funFact: Frasier ran for 11 seasons — the same length as Cheers. Kelsey Grammer played the character for 20 years across both shows.

questions.questionText: How many Primetime Emmy Awards did Cheers win during its run?
questions.funFact: Cheers was nearly canceled after its first season when it ranked 74th out of 96 shows. It went on to become one of TV's most awarded series.

questions.questionText: What was Mark Cooper's career before becoming a teacher in Hangin' with Mr. Cooper?
questions.funFact: In a basketball episode, Mark Curry actually played in a real Golden State Warriors preseason game against the Phoenix Suns.

questions.questionText: In what city is Hangin' with Mr. Cooper set?
questions.funFact: The pilot recycled the Seaver family house set from Growing Pains. Alan Thicke even cameoed as Jason Seaver finding Mark Curry on his couch.

questions.questionText: Who created both Hangin' with Mr. Cooper and Full House?
questions.funFact: Jeff Franklin specialized in family-friendly sitcoms. Both shows aired on ABC's TGIF lineup during the same era.

questions.questionText: Which child actress joined the cast of Hangin' with Mr. Cooper in Season 2?
questions.funFact: Raven-Symoné was already famous from The Cosby Show. She joined when the show shifted to a more family-oriented format.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the community college in Community?
questions.funFact: Dan Harmon based the show on his own experience attending Glendale Community College in California.

questions.questionText: What is the fan slogan that became Community's rallying cry?
questions.funFact: 'Six seasons and a movie' started as an Abed joke. A Community movie was eventually greenlit for Peacock, making the prophecy real.

questions.questionText: What recurring event causes campus-wide chaos in Community?
questions.funFact: The paintball episodes became so popular they turned into annual events. 'Modern Warfare' (Season 1) is consistently rated the show's best episode.

questions.questionText: Which actor plays the eccentric Dean Pelton on Community?
questions.funFact: Jim Rash won an Academy Award for co-writing The Descendants while still filming Community. He showed up to set with his Oscar.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the high school in Saved by the Bell?
questions.funFact: Saved by the Bell started as a completely different show called Good Morning, Miss Bliss on the Disney Channel before being retooled for NBC.

questions.questionText: What is Zack Morris's signature fourth-wall-breaking move on Saved by the Bell?
options: Calling 'Time out!' to freeze the scene
questions.funFact: The 'Time out!' freeze was inspired by Ferris Bueller's Day Off. Mark-Paul Gosselaar was only 15 when the show premiered.

questions.questionText: What is Principal Belding's name a pun on in Saved by the Bell?
questions.funFact: Dennis Haskins played Belding so convincingly that fans would approach him at events calling him 'Mr. Belding' for decades after the show ended.

questions.questionText: Who provides the voiceover narration as Future Ted in How I Met Your Mother?
questions.funFact: Bob Saget never appeared on screen. The child actors' reaction shots were filmed in 2006 before they aged, then reused for all 9 seasons.

questions.questionText: What is Robin Scherbatsky's embarrassing Canadian pop star alter ego in HIMYM?
questions.funFact: The Robin Sparkles music video for 'Let's Go to the Mall' was filmed as a real 1990s-style Canadian pop video and became a viral hit.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the recurring punishment bet between Marshall and Barney in HIMYM?
questions.funFact: Marshall earned the right to slap Barney across the face at any time. The slaps were spread across multiple seasons for maximum comedic impact.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the fictional drinking game the roommates play on New Girl?
questions.funFact: True American's rules were intentionally never fully explained on the show. Fans have attempted to create real playable versions with mixed results.

questions.questionText: What is Jess Day's profession on New Girl?
questions.funFact: The pilot drew 10.28 million viewers — the highest-rated Fox scripted fall debut since 2001.

questions.questionText: What must Schmidt put money into every time he says something douchey on New Girl?
questions.funFact: Max Greenfield was originally cast as a guest star for the pilot. His chemistry with the cast was so strong they made Schmidt a series regular.

questions.questionText: In what fictional Wisconsin town is That '70s Show set?
questions.funFact: Point Place doesn't exist, but the show's creators based it on several small Wisconsin towns they'd visited.

questions.questionText: What is Red Forman's signature threat to Eric on That '70s Show?
options: I'll send you to military school
Wait till your mother hears this
questions.funFact: Kurtwood Smith improvised many variations of the 'foot in your ass' threat. The writers kept a running tally — he said it over 60 times.

questions.questionText: What does 'The Circle' in the Formans' basement represent on That '70s Show?
questions.funFact: The show never explicitly showed marijuana. The Circle used smoke effects and wide-angle lenses to imply what was happening.

questions.questionText: How old was Mila Kunis when she was cast as Jackie on That '70s Show?
questions.funFact: Mila Kunis lied about her age at the audition, saying she'd be 18. The producers didn't find out her real age until after she was cast.

questions.questionText: What radio station does Martin Payne work at in Martin?
questions.funFact: Martin Lawrence based the radio DJ character on real Detroit radio personalities he'd listened to growing up.

questions.questionText: What female character does Martin Lawrence play in drag on Martin?
questions.funFact: Martin played multiple characters including Sheneneh, Mama Payne, Jerome, Otis, and Dragonfly Jones — often appearing in scenes with his own characters.

questions.questionText: In what city is Martin set?
questions.funFact: The show helped popularize phrases like 'You go girl!', 'Talk to the hand', and 'Wazzup' in mainstream American culture.

questions.questionText: What recurring character enters Martin's apartment uninvited through the window?
questions.funFact: Bruh Man always claimed to live 'on the fifth floor' of Martin's building — which clearly didn't have five floors.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the hospital in Scrubs?
questions.funFact: Scrubs was filmed at a real abandoned hospital — North Hollywood Medical Center — giving it an authenticity most sitcoms lack.

questions.questionText: What unique pattern do almost all Scrubs episode titles in seasons 1-8 follow?
options: They all end with a question mark
questions.funFact: The 'My...' format reflects J.D.'s narration — every episode is told from his personal perspective.

questions.questionText: What is the Scrubs theme song?
options: I'm No Superman by Lazlo Bane
Doctor My Eyes by Jackson Browne
questions.funFact: Creator Bill Lawrence based the show on the real residency experiences of his college friend Dr. Jonathan Doris at Brown Medical School.

questions.questionText: What is the Janitor's real name, finally revealed late in Scrubs?
questions.funFact: Neil Flynn improvised most of the Janitor's dialogue. The character was originally supposed to be a figment of J.D.'s imagination.

questions.questionText: What university do the main characters work at in The Big Bang Theory?
questions.funFact: UCLA physicist David Saltzberg served as science consultant. Every equation on the whiteboards is real and scientifically accurate.

questions.questionText: What band performed The Big Bang Theory theme song?
questions.funFact: The full theme song covers the entire history of the universe in under a minute. Most viewers only hear the shortened TV version.

questions.questionText: What is perpetually broken in the apartment building on The Big Bang Theory?
questions.funFact: The broken elevator is explained in a flashback — it broke when a rocket fuel experiment by Howard went wrong. It wasn't fixed until the series finale.

questions.questionText: What lullaby does Sheldon request when he's sick on The Big Bang Theory?
questions.funFact: 'Soft Kitty' became so popular that CBS sold official merchandise. A lawsuit was filed over the lyrics' origin from a 1930s children's song.
